To implement birth notification, the MOHW established the 'Birth Notification Operation Plan' and, after multiple negotiations with the Ministry of the Interior (competent authority for the Child Welfare Act), the MOI finalized and announced the 'Birth Notification Workflow' on 13 September 1994. That December 28 the MOHW promulgated the newly revised 'Birth Certificate' and 'Stillbirth Certificate', and paper-based birth notification began in March 1995. 2. From 2004, medical units switched to online reporting and stopped using paper, while household-registration reporting still used both methods; after continued coordination between the HPA and the MOI's Department of Household Registration, online birth notification was fully implemented from 2005, entirely eliminating paper mailing. 3. On 28 May 2003 the Child Welfare Act and Youth Welfare Act were merged and revised into the Child and Youth Welfare Act, Article 13 of which requires: 'Within 7 days of a fetus's birth, the attendant shall report the birth data to the household-registration and health authorities.' 4. On 30 November 2011 the Child and Youth Welfare and Rights Protection Act was amended, Article 14 requiring: 'Within 7 days of birth, the attendant shall report the birth data to the health authority; the same applies for stillbirths.' For births outside a hospital, clinic, or midwifery clinic where a birth certificate cannot be obtained, a DNA parentage report from a medical institution or a birth-notification form issued by a licensed medical professional must be presented for birth registration. 5. Unlike 'birth registration', 'birth notification' covers all births in Taiwan (regardless of nationality): a. live newborns; b. stillbirths of >=20 weeks' gestation or >=500 g. (Quoted from the HPA's birth-notification background notes.)

Enrollment/disenrollment types: (1) Enroll: joins NHI upon meeting eligibility. (2) Disenroll: 1) death; 2) serving a sentence in prison/detention, or a security/reformatory measure, for 2+ months; 3) missing for 6 months (or from the disaster date if missing due to disaster); 4) becoming an active-duty officer, NCO, soldier, or military-academy funded student (changed to 'transfer out' on 2001-02-01); 5) loss of enrollment conditions (e.g. household moved out, residence permit expired, foreigner's work/study ended and left). (3) Transfer in: 1) change of insurer unit; 2) change of insured identity. (4) Transfer out: 1) change of insurer unit; 2) change of insured identity. (5) Cancel: NHIA cancels a doubly-enrolled insured person. (6) Interrupted transfer in: everyone eligible must enroll; if after enrolling a gap in enrollment arose (job change, identity change, address move, etc.) with unpaid premiums, and the person re-enters NHI. (7) Interrupted transfer out: similarly, a gap leading to exit from NHI. (8) Resume: 1) a missing person found within 6 months should cancel suspension and pay back premiums; if not found after 6 months, insurance is terminated retroactively from the suspension month and disenrollment processed; 2) a person abroad 6+ months resumes on the return date, but one abroad under 6 months cancels suspension and pays back premiums. (9) Suspend: 1) registered missing but under 6 months; 2) continuously detained 2+ months; 3) planned to be abroad 6+ months, except deep-sea fishing-vessel crew; 4) continued-coverage dependents (children, grandchildren) aged 20+ without earning capacity (e.g. disability-certificate holders) or still studying without employment. (10) Suspend-resume: the field changes to 'suspend-resume' when resuming after suspension.
